results.title: matrix: role x operation against auth.audit_log_entries
results.detail: exercised (service_role, authenticated, anon, postgres): service_role=nothing; authenticated=nothing; anon=nothing; postgres=select/insert/update/delete/truncate. NOT exercisable from a postgres session - "permission denied to set role": dashboard_user, supabase_read_only_user; the postgres role is not a member of them, so their privileges are the A01b grant read (dashboard_user holds all five, supabase_read_only_user holds select only) and the Dashboard connects as them directly rather than by SET ROLE. Distinct denial: permission denied for table audit_log_entries | permission denied to set role "dashboard_user" | permission denied to set role "supabase_read_only_user".

results.title: forging an audit entry GoTrue never wrote
results.detail: insert accepted; read back 1 row with a chosen actor (<email>), a chosen source IP and a created_at three days in the past. Removed afterwards: true. The table has no FK to auth.users and no trigger, so nothing reconciles a forged row against a real user.

results.title: rewriting an existing entry in place (source IP and action)
results.detail: UPDATE accepted: the row's source IP and its action were both rewritten (1 row now reads action=logout from 10.0.0.1). An audit row is a plain heap row - no immutability, no version, no updated_at to notice the edit by. Table left at 0 rows.
